newsitem.title: USA: US inner cities face severe credit shortage -- Rubin.
newsitem.headline: US inner cities face severe credit shortage -- Rubin.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Friday that America's inner cities face a "severe" shortage of credit and called for a national effort to help them.

"We ... have a severe shortage of credit and financial institutions willing to provide credit to build housing and create jobs in the inner city," he said in a speech prepared for delivery to the Conference of Mayors here.
Rubin said that the Clinton administration has an eight-point program to help right that problem through empowerment zones and other measures.
It is also working on ways to bring into the banking system the 10 million Americans who receive Social Security, veterans or government checks but do not have bank accounts.
That would not only give those people "a better way to access services, but it may also encourage them to save, to plan financially and thus, to improve their economic life over time," Rubin said.

As he has done before, the Treasury chief argued that America as a whole loses out as long as residents of the inner cities remain out of the economic mainstream. "We need a true marshaling of national will and effort" to help them, he said.
